description: The image presents three side-by-side horizontal bar charts titled “Understanding,” “Reasoning,” and “Trustworthiness,” illustrating the performance of various large language models on these dimensions, as part of the evaluation in the paper “A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models.” Each chart displays model names along the vertical axis, sorted in descending order of performance within that category, and performance scores (as percentages) along the horizontal axis, ranging from 0% to 100% with tick marks at 20% intervals. In the “Understanding” chart, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 leads with 98.0%, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M (91.7%) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M (87.1%), while Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct trails at 2.4%. The “Reasoning” chart shows gpt-4o-2024-11-20 again at the top with 66.5%, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M (58.0%), and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct at 7.2%. In the “Trustworthiness” chart, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 achieves the highest score of 88.8%, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M (71.8%) and gpt-4o-2024-11-20 (54.6%), while Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct scores 0.0%. Each bar is colored in varying shades of blue, with darker shades generally corresponding to higher-performing models, and exact numerical scores are labeled at the end of each bar. The charts collectively highlight gpt-4o variants and Qwen2.5 models as top performers across all three metrics, while smaller Llama and Phi models consistently score lower.
